messages.subject: read.morphologika no longer working
parts:
Hi, 

I'm finding that read.morphologika is no longer working in R (R v. 4.1.1 or R v 4.2.2) I have the 4.0.4 version of geomorph. 

I also tried loading separately the source for read.morphologika from the v.4.0.0 geomorph source, but I still couldn't get the function to work (this is in R v.4.1.1).  I originally wrote my working script in this version of R and geomorph,  so I'm not sure why this isn't working.

Is there a way to load the full geomorph v4.0.0 package in R/RStudio? Admittedly I don't know how to load the full package from the source code. 

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: read.morphologika no longer working
parts:
Apologies for multiple posts! I got geomorph 4.0.0 installed and I am using R 4.1.1 (which are the versions I used when I originally wrote this script, and it definitely worked).

> filelist <- list.files(pattern = ".txt")
> mydata <- read.morphologika(filelist)
Error in rbind(coords, two.d.array(temp)) :

Any ideas?

Thanks!

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] read.morphologika no longer working
parts:
Dear Katie,

It is difficult to replicate read.morphologika errors because errors are usually dependent on the files that are in a specific directory on one’s computer.  This function has not been updated in a long time.  I was able to verify the function works with a morphologika file I found online, saved in a fresh directory, and I was able to verify if an alternative .txt file was added to that directory, the function caught that it was not a morpholgika-formatted file.  Note that this is an old function that basically provides a loop to use an internal function, read.one.morphologika, binding each set of landmark data from each file onto a growing matrix, which is converted into an array at the end.  The error you received indicates that one of the files has a different number of landmarks (or landmarks in more or fewer dimensions) than the files that preceded it.  The function could do a better job of indicating with which file the reading of data was arrested, but that would mean the error would still be triggered, even if a better explanation could be offered.

If I were in your shoes, I would create a new empty directory, copy and add one file from the other directory, and make sure the function works after creating a file list with just one file.  Then I would copy the files, one by one, from the other directory and re-run until I determined which file caused the error, so I could investigate what is going on with that particular file.

There are a few possible explanations.  One is that you might have added new files to the directory since the time it worked, or altered some files within (even if not intentional)  Another is that R could have changed something with its scan function that is the workhorse for any read.something function, and certain files might trigger a problem that was not there before the alteration.  This is just a guess — don’t know the history of scan updates.  It is also possible updates to strsplit or grep function in R were made.

Unfortunately, a trial and error approach will be needed to better determine which file or files cause errors.  I hope it is a simple change to the file list on your end, as that would be easy to fix.  This function has not been updated since 2017 so it is likely not a geomorph change that caused your error.  Hopefully it is not an incompatible R update.

Best,
Mike

Luckily I had the landmarks saved in a csv file (written from my previous 3darray), so I'm using that for now (which works fine after a bit coercing into the right format for gpagen). This is a good reminder to me to have a "don't touch" backup copy of raw data! 

Thank you again!
Katie

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] read.morphologika no longer working
parts:
Although morphologika files, like tps or nts files, as well, contain the values for Cartesian coordinates, and are, therefore, possible data repositories, I feel read.morphologika should be used only once for the express purpose of acquiring data that could be saved in a more reasonable format, including csv files or Rdata objects.  Whether you recover your ability to acquire data from your morphologika files or are happy with the coercion effort, I recommend saving all of the objects you wish to work with again (using the save function) as an Rdata object.  Then your script can simply use the load function to reload the various data, and possibly, saved analyses.  Rdata objects should be more robust with respect to the changes R makes, and won’t care if you mangle text files along the way.

Cheers!
Mike
